chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl from Aban ibn Taghlib who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I say to her when I am alone with her?' He said, 'You should say: I marry you for a mut'ah (temporary marriage) according to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), not as an inheritor nor as an inherited one, for such and such a day, and if you wish, such and such a year, for such and such a dirham, and you specify the term, whether it be little or much, whatever you two agree upon. When she says 'Yes', she is pleased, and she is your wife, and you are the most entitled of people to her.' I said, 'But I am shy to mention the condition of the days.' He said, 'It is more detrimental to you.' I said, 'How so?' He said, 'Indeed, if you do not stipulate it, it becomes a permanent marriage, necessitating maintenance upon you during the waiting period, and she becomes an inheritor, and you cannot divorce her except with a Sunnah divorce.'

key_terms.لَا مَوْرُوثَةً: Not as an inherited one (referring to the husband not inheriting from the wife in mut'ah)
key_terms.لَا وَارِثَةً: Not as an inheritor (referring to the wife not inheriting from the husband in mut'ah)

ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences of omitting the duration in a temporary marriage contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the legal mechanics of mut'ah, emphasizing that explicit stipulation of duration is crucial to distinguish it from permanent marriage (nikah muqam). The Imam explains that omitting the time period defaults the contract to permanence, thereby obligating maintenance during the iddah and granting inheritance rights, which necessitates a formal divorce (talaq al-sunnah) rather than the flexibility of temporary marriage. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that mut'ah is a distinct contractual category requiring precise verbal formulation to avoid unintended permanent status.
